validity.recommendation: Correct Diameter from '20, 24, 36' to '20, 24, 30' -- no 36-inch pipe was ever part of this project.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Diameter = '20, 24, 36' (in). Two independent FERC-derived government documents state the diameter set explicitly and consistently, and neither contains a 36-inch segment: (1) FERC's Jan 2010 Notice of Public Scoping Meetings (Docket PF09-15-000), 'Summary of the Planned Project': 'DTI plans to construct and operate approximately 110 miles of 20-, 24-, and 30-inch diameter natural gas pipeline' -- itemized as ~43.1 mi of 30-inch (Marshall Co. WV / Greene Co. PA), ~54.2 mi of 24-inch (Greene/Washington/Allegheny/Westmoreland Cos. PA), ~5.2 mi of 20-inch loop (Kanawha Co. WV) and 6 mi of 24-inch loop (Greene Co. PA) = 110.0 mi exactly, matching GEM's LengthKnown. (2) FERC's April 2011 Notice of Availability of the EA (Docket CP10-448-000) restates it after the formal application: 'authorization to construct and operate ... 110 miles of 20- through 30-inch-diameter pipeline (26.3 miles in West Virginia and 74.9 miles in Pennsylvania)' and itemizes 8 pipeline facilities by exact diameter: 20-in (TL-570 Ext.1, 5.3 mi, Kanawha Co. WV), 24-in (TL-492 Ext.5, 6 mi, Greene Co. PA), 30-in (TL-590, 42.3 mi, Marshall/Greene Cos.), 24-in (TL-591, 54.2 mi, Greene/Washington/Allegheny/Westmoreland Cos. PA), 16-in x3 (TL-596/598/599, 0.5+0.3+0.4 mi, WV), 10-in (TL-597, 0.1 mi, WV). No FERC document at any stage of this docket (pre-filing scoping through the pre-construction EA) mentions a 36-inch segment. The '36' in GEM's current value looks like a transposition of '30' (a 3-6 vs 3-0 slip), not a real spec. Opened and read to exhaustion: both Federal Register notices (full text), the Harvard ELR appendix table entry for CP10-448 (confirms docket/date only, no diameter), the Construction Equipment Guide article and the Dominion press release (neither states per-segment diameter, only general trench-depth language for 30-36in pipe in the CEG piece, which is DOT burial-depth boilerplate, not a claim about this project's diameter).

validity.recommendation: No existence/classification/duplicate action needed; see the spec and attribution concerns above for the two cell-level fixes found.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of GEM and of Dominion's own messaging. FERC ran this project through public pre-filing (Docket PF09-15-000, Notice of Intent 12/14/2009), public scoping meetings (Jan 2010, 4 meetings named with addresses/dates), a formal Section 7(c) application filed 6/1/2010 (Docket CP10-448-000, cost estimate $633,757,763, 17,965 hp of new/upgraded compression), an Environmental Assessment (April 2011), and a certificate order (135 FERC PP61,239 / 136 FERC PP61,031, approved 6/16/2011) -- independently confirmed by the Harvard Environmental Law Review's compiled table of FERC-approved pipeline projects (Gocke appendix), a wholly separate origin from Dominion. The Construction Equipment Guide trade article and Dominion's own Sept 2012 in-service press release (mirrored on PRNewswire) corroborate the in-service date and are consistent with, though not fully independent of, the government record. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as an operating interstate gas transmission project; Dominion Transmission Inc. is the FERC-jurisdictional operator (matches Owner1=Dominion Energy, the parent). DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against the full 46-row roster -- no overlap. The only name-adjacent row is P0153 'Appalachian Connector Pipeline' (Columbia/TCO, 52 mi, ?->Chatham, cap 2000 MMcf/d), which is a distinct, unrelated project (different operator family, different mileage, different capacity, different route) -- not a duplicate or mislabel of P2502. SPEC (confirmed, not just mentioned -- the numbers agree): Length 110 mi matches both FERC notices' segment-by-segment sums (110.0 mi in the 2010 scoping notice, ~109.1 mi in the 2011 EA's itemization, difference is minor unenumerated 'associated minor pipeline'). Capacity 484.26 (GEM's MMcf/d field) matches '484,260 dekatherms per day' stated identically in the 2010 FERC scoping notice, the 2011 FERC EA notice, the CEG article and Dominion's release (dekatherms and Mcf are treated as equivalent in this GEM field convention; not flagging as a units error). SegmentCost 635,000,000 USD is within ~0.2% of FERC's own application estimate of $633,757,763 (govinfo.gov FR-2010-06-21 Notice of Application) -- close enough to read as the same figure rounded/updated, not a material disagreement. ConstructionYear=2011 and StartYear1=2012 are consistent with the FERC timeline (certificate 6/16/2011; in-service 9/4/2012 per Dominion/CEG) -- the exact in-service date rests on Dominion-origin material only (this batch's second-source search for a fully independent confirmation of the Sept 2012 date did not turn one up before the session's web-search budget was exhausted; flagging as medium tier on StartYear1 rather than high). Opened and read in full: both Federal Register notices, the govinfo.gov Notice of Application PDF (via pdftotext), the Harvard ELR appendix table, the CEG article, and the Dominion/PRNewswire release -- 5 of this row's 3 harvested wiki citations were opened (the EIA generic data.php landing page was also attempted but timed out twice and does not name this pipeline specifically; not usable as a ref for existence or any value).

summary: P2502 Appalachian Gateway Pipeline: existence, classification, ownership, length, capacity and cost all confirmed independently via 2 FERC/Federal Register notices + an academic FERC-order compilation + trade press/operator release (no duplicate on the 46-row roster); staged REFS_ADDED fills for Status/Fuel/Construction/Start/Capacity/Length/FuelSource/Location/SegmentCost/Operator/Owner and new values for ProposalYear/Month and EndLocation. Two concerns filed with contested candidates: Diameter should be '20, 24, 30' not '20, 24, 36' (no 36-inch segment exists in any FERC filing), and 'West Virgina' should read 'West Virginia' in StartState/Province and FuelSource.
